points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 拜伦出生于伦敦一个没落的贵族家庭，父亲是海军军官，母亲是苏格兰人。他天生跛足，这一生理缺陷影响了他的性格形成。早年丧父，母亲性格乖戾，家庭关系紧张。这段经历使拜伦敏感早熟，同时也培养了他对自由的渴望和对权威的反抗精神。他在伦敦接受了早期教育，展现出非凡的文学天赋。
points.descriptionEn: Byron was born in London into a declining noble family; his father was a naval officer and his mother Scottish. Born with a clubfoot, this physical defect influenced his personality development. Orphaned early, his mother had a difficult temperament, creating a tense family environment. This experience made Byron sensitive and precocious, while also cultivating his desire for freedom and rebellious spirit against authority. He received early education in London, showing extraordinary literary talent.

points.title: 大学启蒙
points.description: 拜伦进入剑桥大学三一学院学习，但学业并不突出。他大量阅读文学、历史和哲学著作，尤其受到启蒙思想的影响。在此期间，他开始创作诗歌，并积累了大量债务。他还养成了游泳、拳击等运动习惯，以弥补身体缺陷。这段时期奠定了他的文学基础，也塑造了他后来的生活方式——放荡不羁却又充满创造力。
points.descriptionEn: Byron entered Trinity College, Cambridge, but his academic performance was not outstanding. He extensively read literature, history, and philosophy, particularly influenced by Enlightenment ideas. During this time, he began writing poetry and accumulated substantial debts. He also developed habits like swimming and boxing to compensate for his physical disability. This period laid his literary foundation and shaped his later lifestyle—licentious yet full of creativity.

points.title: 欧陆漫游
points.description: 拜伦开始了为期两年的欧洲大陆旅行，先后到访葡萄牙、西班牙、马耳他、阿尔巴尼亚、希腊等地。这段旅行极大地开阔了他的视野，激发了他对异国文化的浓厚兴趣。他在伊比利亚半岛见证了拿破仑战争，在希腊接触到古典文明，这些经历成为他日后创作的重要素材。旅行期间，他创作了《恰尔德·哈罗尔德游记》的前两章，这部作品使他一举成名，确立了他在英国文坛的地位。
points.descriptionEn: Byron embarked on a two-year European tour, visiting Portugal, Spain, Malta, Albania, Greece and other places. This journey greatly broadened his horizons and sparked his deep interest in foreign cultures. He witnessed the Napoleonic Wars in the Iberian Peninsula and encountered classical civilization in Greece, experiences that became important material for his later works. During the journey, he wrote the first two cantos of 'Childe Harold's Pilgrimage,' which brought him immediate fame and established his position in British literary circles.

points.title: 文坛崛起
points.description: 回到伦敦后，拜伦迅速成为社交界的宠儿，他的诗歌广受欢迎。他发表了《恰尔德·哈罗尔德游记》后两章以及一系列东方叙事诗，如《阿比多斯的新娘》、《海盗》等，这些作品展现了他独特的浪漫主义风格。然而，他的私生活备受争议，与多位女性有染，包括他的异母姐姐奥古斯塔·利。这些丑闻导致他声誉受损，最终在1816年被迫离开英国，开始了流亡生活。
points.descriptionEn: Back in London, Byron quickly became a darling of society, and his poems gained widespread popularity. He published the remaining cantos of 'Childe Harold's Pilgrimage' and a series of oriental narrative poems such as 'The Bride of Abydos' and 'The Corsair,' showcasing his unique romantic style. However, his private life was controversial, with affairs with multiple women including his half-sister Augusta Leigh. These scandals damaged his reputation, eventually forcing him to leave England in 1816 and begin an exile.

points.title: 流亡与革命
points.description: 拜伦先在瑞士居住，后移居意大利，在威尼斯、拉韦纳等地生活。在意大利，他创作了《唐·璜》等代表作，这部讽刺史诗被誉为英国文学史上最伟大的作品之一。同时，他积极参与希腊独立运动，投入大量资金支持希腊反抗奥斯曼帝国的斗争。1823年，他亲自前往希腊，加入希腊独立军，担任总司令。次年，因热病去世，年仅36岁。拜伦之死使他成为希腊民族英雄，他的遗体被运回英国安葬，但心脏被保存在希腊，成为希腊独立运动的象征。
points.descriptionEn: Byron first lived in Switzerland, then moved to Italy, residing in Venice, Ravenna and other places. In Italy, he created masterpieces like 'Don Juan,' considered one of the greatest works in English literary history. Simultaneously, he actively participated in the Greek independence movement, investing substantial funds to support Greece's struggle against the Ottoman Empire. In 1823, he traveled to Greece personally, joining the Greek independence army as commander-in-chief. The following year, he died of fever at the age of 36. Byron's death made him a national hero of Greece, and while his body was returned to England for burial, his heart was preserved in Greece, becoming a symbol of the Greek independence movement.

appraisal.zh: 拜伦被公认为浪漫主义文学的代表人物，诗作激情洋溢、反抗精神强烈，《唐·璜》被誉为英国文学史上最伟大的讽刺诗之一，其投身希腊独立更使他成为自由与正义的象征。不过也有研究者指出，他生活放荡、道德观念薄弱，与异母姐的关系尤受谴责，诗作过于个人化，对希腊的支援更多出于个人英雄主义与浪漫幻想，贵族出身也使他难以真正体察底层疾苦。无论如何，他将个人命运与时代精神相结合，其名字已成为跨越时代的文化符号。
appraisal.en: Byron is widely recognized as a representative figure of Romantic literature: his poetry brims with passion and rebellion, 'Don Juan' is hailed as one of the greatest satirical poems in English, and his commitment to Greek independence made him a symbol of freedom and justice. Yet some researchers note that his life was dissolute and his morals weak, his relationship with his half-sister especially condemned; his poetry is seen as overly personal, and his Greek cause as personal heroism and romantic fantasy rather than true understanding of the people, his noble birth distancing him from common suffering. Still, he fused personal destiny with the spirit of his age, and his name has become a cultural symbol across eras.

supporter.zh: 拜伦被视为浪漫主义文学的伟大先驱，他的诗歌充满激情与反抗精神，对后世文学产生深远影响。他敢于挑战社会规范，追求个人自由，这种精神激励了无数后来者。他的作品《唐·璜》被誉为英国文学史上最伟大的讽刺诗之一，而他对希腊独立的支持则体现了他崇高的人道主义情怀。拜伦不仅是诗人，更是自由与正义的象征，他的生命短暂却充满传奇色彩。
supporter.en: Byron is regarded as a great pioneer of Romantic literature, whose poetry is filled with passion and rebellious spirit, profoundly influencing later literature. He dared to challenge social norms and pursue personal freedom, inspiring countless successors. His work 'Don Juan' is hailed as one of the greatest satirical poems in English literary history, while his support for Greek independence reflects his noble humanitarian spirit. Byron was not just a poet but a symbol of freedom and justice, his life though short, was filled with legendary color.

critic.zh: 批评者认为拜伦的生活放荡不羁，道德观念薄弱，与异母姐的不伦关系尤其受到谴责。他的诗歌被认为过于个人化，缺乏深刻的社会关怀。此外，他对希腊独立的支持也被质疑为个人英雄主义的表现，而非真正理解希腊人民的诉求。拜伦的贵族身份使他难以真正理解底层民众的疾苦，他的革命热情更多源于浪漫幻想而非对现实的深刻理解。
critic.en: Critics argue that Byron's life was dissolute with weak moral principles, particularly condemned for his incestuous relationship with his half-sister. His poetry is considered overly personal, lacking deep social concern. Additionally, his support for Greek independence is questioned as an expression of personal heroism rather than genuine understanding of the Greek people's aspirations. Byron's noble background made it difficult for him to truly understand the suffering of the common people, and his revolutionary enthusiasm stemmed more from romantic fantasy than profound understanding of reality.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，拜伦被公认为浪漫主义文学的代表人物，他的作品融合了个人情感与社会批判。他的生平反映了19世纪初欧洲知识分子的精神状态——既追求个人解放，又关注社会变革。拜伦的形象在流行文化中被不断重塑，从拜伦式英雄到反叛偶像，他的名字已成为一种文化符号。他的遗产不仅在于文学成就，更在于他如何将个人命运与时代精神相结合，成为跨越时代的文化现象。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Byron is widely recognized as a representative figure of Romantic literature, whose works blend personal emotion with social criticism. His life reflects the spiritual state of European intellectuals in the early 19th century—pursuing both personal liberation and social change. Byron's image has been continuously reshaped in popular culture, from the Byronic hero to the rebellious icon, his name becoming a cultural symbol. His legacy lies not only in literary achievements but in how he combined personal destiny with the spirit of the times, becoming a cultural phenomenon that transcends eras.

self.zh: 我宁愿做我自己，也不愿做宇宙的模仿者。
self.en: I would rather be myself than mimic the universe.
